 |title= Where is the Freedom to Question?

 |archive-date= 2012-08-17
 |url-status= dead

}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal

 |journal=The African Review of Physics

==Education==
Wayne completed his undergraduate studies in botany at the [[University of Massachusetts]]. He earned an M.A. in biology from the [[University of California at Los Angeles]], and a Ph.D. in Plant Cell Biology from the [[University of Massachusetts]] in 1985 working under [[Peter K. Hepler]]. He was a post-doc at The [[University of Texas at Austin]] working with Stanley Roux, Guy Thompson, and H. Y. Lim Tung, and had a Japanese Society for the Promotion of Science Fellowship to work with Masashi Tazawa at the [[University of Tokyo]]. While in Japan, Wayne worked at the [[National Institute for Basic Biology, Japan|National Institute of Basic Biology]] in Okazaki with Akeo Kadota, Masakatsu Watanabe, and Masaki Furuya, [[Hitotsubashi University]] in Kunitachi with Eiji Kamitsubo, and the [[Himeji Institute of Technology]] with Tetsuro Mimura and Teruo Shimmen.{{citation needed|date=September 2022}}

== Career ==
Wayne joined the faculty at [[Cornell University]] in 1987. He is a member of the CALS School of Integrative Plant Science.<ref>{{cite web |title=School of Integrative Plant Science |url=https://cals.cornell.edu/school-integrative-plant-science |access-date=March 28, 2019}}</ref> He has a deep interest in teaching science <ref>{{cite journal | last=Mazhar|first=Tajwar | title=Prof's Book Blurs Boundaries between Sciences | journal=Cornell Daily Sun |date=November 4, 2009 | url=http://cornellsun.com/node/39403}}</ref> and teaches Plant Cell Biology and Light and Video Microscopy. He has taught a course for nonmajors entitled, Biological Principles <ref>{{cite web |last1=Wayne |first1=Randy |title=Biological Principles |url=https://labs.plantbio.cornell.edu/wayne/teaching.html |website=Randy Wayne's World |access-date=March 10, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last=Newkirk|first=Zach | title=Freedom to Teach at Cornell. | journal =Cornell Progressive | volume=11 | issue=4| pages=1, 5 | year=2011 | url=http://cuprogressive.files.wordpress.com/2011/08/progressive_nov_19.pdf}}</ref> and subsequently taught a course for nonmajors entitled, Light and Life.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Wayne |first1=Randy |title=Complete Set of Notes 2022 |url=https://labs.plantbio.cornell.edu/wayne/pdfs/CompleteLightandLifeNotes2022.pdf |website=Randy Wayne's World |access-date=July 1, 2022}}</ref> Wayne also has strong views on the meaning of a college education.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Wayne |first1=Randy |title=Putting the Measurable over the Meaningful. Letter to the Editor |url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/magazine/2019/03/01/letters/T0RTlAFtpSxVv6xEfdHbnO/story.html |access-date=November 11, 2019 |work=Boston Globe Magazine |date= March 1, 2019}}</ref> Wayne is a member of the Biology and Society major,<ref>{{cite web |title=Biology & Society Major at Cornell University |url=https://sts.cornell.edu/bio-society |publisher=Department of Science & Technology Studies at Cornell University |access-date=March 17, 2019}}</ref> which is designed for students who wish to combine training in biology with perspectives from the social sciences and humanities to understand the scientific, social, political, and ethical aspects of modern biology.

===Fern spore germination===

When it was generally assumed that fern spores contained all the ions necessary for germination,<ref>{{cite book|last=Raghavan|first=V|title=Cytology, Physiology, and Biochemistry of Germination of Fern Spores|series=International Review of Cytology|year=1980|volume=62|pages=69–118|doi=10.1016/S0074-7696(08)61899-9|isbn=9780123644626}}</ref>  Wayne, working with [[Peter K. Hepler]], showed that external [[calcium ions]] were necessary for the red light-stimulated, [[phytochrome]]-mediated signal transduction chain that leads to the [[germination]] response of the spores of ''Onoclea sensibilis''.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Wayne|first1=Randy |last2=Hepler|first2=Peter, K. | title=The Role of Calcium Ions in Phytochrome-mediated germination of spores of Onoclea sensibilis L. | journal=Planta | volume=160 | issue=1 | pages=12–20 | year=1984 | pmid=24258366 | doi=10.1007/BF00392460 | bibcode=1984Plant.160...12W | s2cid=14789256 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Wayne|first1=Randy|last2=Hepler|first2=Peter K. | title=Red Light Stimulates and Increase in Intracellular Calcium in the Spores of Onoclea sensibilis. | journal=Plant Physiology | volume=77 | issue=1 | pages=8–11 | year=1985 |url =http://www.plantphysiol.org/content/77/1/8.full.pdf/| pmid=16664033 | pmc=1064446 | doi=10.1104/pp.77.1.8}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Wayne|first1=Randy |last2=Hepler|first2=Peter K. | title=The Atomic Composition of Onoclea sensibilis Spores. | journal=American Fern Journal | volume=75 | issue=1 | pages=12–18 | year=1985 | doi=10.2307/1546574 | jstor=1546574 | bibcode=1985AmFJ...75...12W | url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/part/230521 }}</ref>

===Water permeability of plant cell membranes===

It was generally considered that water moved in and out of the plant cell through the [[lipid bilayer]]. Wayne, working with [[Masashi Tazawa]],<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Wayne|first1=Randy|last2=Tazawa|first2=Masashi| title=Nature of the Water Channels in the Internodal Cells of Nitellopsis. | journal=Journal of Membrane Biology | volume=116 | pages=31–39 | year=1990 | issue=1 | doi=10.1007/bf01871669| pmid=2165174 | s2cid=15863712 }}</ref> presented most of the now classical arguments favoring membrane water channels and clearly demonstrated their major contribution to osmotic water transport.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Maurel|first=Christophe|title=Aquaporins and Water Permeability of Plant Membranes|journal=Annual Review of Plant Physiology and Plant Molecular Biology|year=1997|volume=48|pages=399–429|doi=10.1146/annurev.arplant.48.1.399|pmid=15012269}}</ref> Wayne's work preceded the molecular identification of [[aquaporins]] in plant cells.<ref name="pmid17875436">{{cite book | author = Kaldenhoff, R., Bertl, A., Otto, B., Moshelion, M. and Uehlein, N. | title = Osmosensing and Osmosignaling | chapter = Characterization of Plant Aquaporins | volume = 428 | pages = 505–31 | year = 2007 | pmid = 17875436 | doi = 10.1016/S0076-6879(07)28028-0 | series = Methods in Enzymology | isbn = 9780123739216 }}</ref><ref name="pmid7920711">{{cite journal | author = Kammerloher, W., Fischer, U., Piechottka, G.P. and Schäffner, A.R. | title = Water Channels in the Plant Plasma Membrane Cloned by Immunoselection from a Mammalian Expression System | journal = Plant J. | volume = 6 | issue = 2 | pages = 187–99 | year = 1994 | pmid = 7920711 | doi = 10.1046/j.1365-313X.1994.6020187.x | doi-access = free }}</ref><ref name="pmid11337406">{{cite journal | author = Maeshima, M. | title = Tonoplast Transporters: Organization and Function | journal = Annual Review of Plant Physiology and Plant Molecular Biology | volume = 52 | issue = 1| pages = 469–497 | year = 2001 | pmid = 11337406 | doi = 10.1146/annurev.arplant.52.1.469 }}</ref>

===Gravity sensing in plant cells===

It is generally believed that the sedimentation of starch-containing [[plastids]], known as [[amyloplasts]], is responsible for gravity-sensing in plant cells.<ref>{{cite journal | last=Morita|first=Miyo T.| title=Directional Gravity Sensing in Gravitropism. | journal=Annual Review of Plant Biology | volume=61 | pages=705–720 | year=2010 | issue=1 |url =http://xa.yimg.com/kq/groups/17623528/1674519244/name/Morita+2010+gravitropism.pdf | doi=10.1146/annurev.arplant.043008.092042 | pmid=19152486| bibcode=2010AnRPB..61..705M }}</ref> However, based on the facts that plant cells that do not contain sedimenting [[amyloplasts]] still sense gravity<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Wayne|first1=Randy|last2=Staves|first2=Mark P.|last3=Leopold|first3=A. Carl | title=Detection of Gravity-Induced Polarity of Cytoplasmic Streaming in Chara. | journal=Protoplasma | volume=188 | pages=38–48 | year=1995 | issue=1–2 | doi=10.1007/BF01276794 | pmid=11539183 | s2cid=14988993 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Wayne|first1=Randy|last2=Staves|first2=Mark P. | title=A Down-to-Earth Model of Gravisensing or Newton's Law of Gravitation from the Apple's Perspective. | journal=Physiologia Plantarum | volume=98 | issue=4 | pages=917–921 | year=1996 | doi=10.1111/j.1399-3054.1996.tb06703.x | pmid=11539338 | bibcode=1996PPlan..98..917W }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Wayne|first1=Randy|last2=Staves|first2=Mark P.|last3=Leopold|first3=A. Carl | title=The Contribution of the Extracellular Matrix to Gravisensing in Characean Cells. | journal=Journal of Cell Science | volume=101 | pages=611–623 | year=1992 | issue=3 | doi=10.1242/jcs.101.3.611 | pmid=1522145 |url =http://jcs.biologists.org/content/101/3/611.full.pdf}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Wayne|first1=Randy|last2=Staves|first2=Mark P.|last3=Leopold|first3=A. Carl | title=The Effect of the External Medium on the Gravity-Induced Polarity of Cytoplasmic Streaming in Chara corallina (Characeae). | journal=American Journal of Botany | volume=84 | pages=1516–1521 | year=1997 | issue=11 | doi=10.2307/2446612 | jstor=2446612 | pmid=11541058 }}</ref> and that starchless mutants in higher plants are almost as sensitive to gravity as the wild-type plants,<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Casper|first1=Timothy|last2=Pickard|first2=Barbara G.| title=Gravitropism in a Starchless Mutant of Arabidopsis: Implications for the Starch-Statolith Theory of Gravity Sensing. | journal=Planta | volume=177 | pages=185–197 | year=1989 | issue=2 | doi=10.1007/BF00392807 | pmid=24212341 | bibcode=1989Plant.177..185C | s2cid=3703387 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Weise|first1=Sean E.|last2=Kiss|first2=John H.| title=Gravitropism of Influorescence Stems in Starch-Deficient Mutants of Arabidopsis. | journal=International Journal of Plant Sciences | volume=160 | issue=3 | pages=521–527 | year=1999 | doi=10.1086/314142 | pmid=11542271 | s2cid=21480340 }}</ref> Wayne, working with [[Mark P. Staves]] and [[A. Carl Leopold]] proposed that the amyloplasts do not act as gravity sensors, but as a ballast to enhance the gravitational pressure sensed by proteins at the [[plasma membrane]]–[[extracellular matrix]] junction.<ref name=NYTSciWatch/><ref name=WaPo/><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Wayne|first1=Randy|last2=Staves|first2=Mark P.|last3=Leopold|first3=A. Carl | title=The Effect of the External Medium on the Gravitropic Curvature of Rice (ORYZA SATIVA, POACEAE) Roots. | journal=American Journal of Botany | volume=84 | pages=1522–1529 | year=1997 | issue=11 | doi=10.2307/2446613 | jstor=2446613 | pmid=11541059 | doi-access=free | bibcode=1997AmJB...84.1522S }}</ref>
